fabrics.name: Network
fabrics.definition: Connectivity delivered as a service: TCL's Network Fabric (IZO). Global VPN and MPLS, internet access, private lines and IP transit over TCL's subsea and terrestrial fibre; SD-WAN and internet WAN; multi-cloud connectivity and networking; data-centre connectivity; managed Wi-Fi, LAN and enterprise broadband; network-as-a-service with on-demand, programmable control; network APIs, SDN/NFV, satellite integration, and optical and photonic transport.
fabrics.tcl_today: IZO network services, sold globally: global VPN and MPLS, internet access, private lines, IP transit, SD-WAN and internet WAN, multi-cloud connectivity and multi-cloud networking, data-centre connectivity, managed Wi-Fi and LAN, enterprise broadband in India, and network-as-a-service. Assets: 1,500+ PoPs; 500,000+ km of subsea and 200,000+ km of terrestrial fibre; about 35% of global internet traffic routed on its network; ISP partners in 230+ countries. Wholesale carrier services: IPX, roaming, voice termination; 15% of global voice traffic and 1 in 7 international calls. Recognition: a leader in Gartner's Magic Quadrant for Global WAN Services for 13 years; IDC, Avasant and ISG leader for managed SD-WAN/SASE and network services. Customers include Seaco, Noble Resources and Clariant. Sources: https://www.tatacommunications.com/izo, https://www.tatacommunications.com/carrier-services Company-wide: about 5,000 enterprise customers, including 300 of the Fortune 500, in 190+ countries; part of the Tata Group.
fabrics.open_question: Confirm this definition and the TCL-today profile, both taken from tatacommunications.com on 4 Oct 2026, with TCL stakeholders.

fabrics.name: Cloud
fabrics.definition: Enterprise cloud and AI infrastructure: TCL's Cloud Fabric (Vayu). AI cloud with on-demand GPUs and an AI development platform; private, hybrid, multi-cloud and edge computing; sovereign and industry clouds (government, financial services) that keep data in-country; compute, storage, backup and disaster recovery, databases, DevOps and observability; data platforms for integration, governance and analytics.
fabrics.tcl_today: Vayu Cloud, sold in India only: AI cloud with on-demand NVIDIA GPUs and the Vayu AI Studio platform; private, hybrid and multi-cloud; edge (Vayu Edge); a government community cloud and a financial-services cloud; compute (virtual machines, Kubernetes), storage, backup and disaster recovery, managed databases, DevOps and observability; the Vayu Data Platform. Claims: sovereign by design (data and metadata stay in India), compliance with RBI, IRDAI, SEBI and MeitY rules, ISO/IEC 42001, about 30% lower total cost (IDC). Recognition: ISG leader for private/hybrid cloud and data-centre services. Customers include Tata CLiQ, InterGlobe and BACL. Partners: AWS, Microsoft, NVIDIA. Source: https://www.tatacommunications.com/cloud Company-wide: about 5,000 enterprise customers, including 300 of the Fortune 500, in 190+ countries; part of the Tata Group.
fabrics.open_question: Confirm this definition and the TCL-today profile, both taken from tatacommunications.com on 4 Oct 2026, with TCL stakeholders.

fabrics.name: Security
fabrics.definition: Cyber security and resilience: TCL's Security Fabric. Secure access service edge (SASE), security service edge (SSE) and zero-trust network access; managed detection and response and security operations centres; cloud security; operational-technology (OT) security; DDoS protection and advanced network security; security assessment, governance, risk and compliance; threat intelligence.
fabrics.tcl_today: Security Fabric: managed and hosted SASE (hosted SASE powered by Versa), security service edge, zero-trust network access, managed detection and response with security operations centres, cloud security, OT security, advanced network security and DDoS protection, security assessment and governance, risk and compliance consulting, quarterly threat advisories, and an Edge Distribution Platform combining CDN, security and compute. Scale: 9.5 billion events screened a day, 3.5 TBps of traffic screened, 900+ threat-detection use cases. Recognition: KuppingerCole overall leader for MDR (2026); IDC MarketScape leader for Asia/Pacific managed SD-WAN/SASE. Customers include OSN, Liberty General Insurance and vHealth by Aetna. Source: https://www.tatacommunications.com/cyber-security-solutions Company-wide: about 5,000 enterprise customers, including 300 of the Fortune 500, in 190+ countries; part of the Tata Group.
fabrics.open_question: New on 4 Oct: TCL's site names a Security Fabric. Security moved here from Cloud's definition; confirm the scope with TCL stakeholders.

fabrics.name: Interaction
fabrics.definition: How enterprises and their customers communicate: TCL's Interaction Fabric (Kaleyra and Commotion). Communications platforms as a service (messaging, voice and video APIs), contact centre as a service, unified communications and collaboration, cloud voice and SIP trunking; conversational and voice AI, AI agents that complete enterprise workflows, and customer-experience platforms.
fabrics.tcl_today: Kaleyra and Commotion: communications platforms as a service (messaging, voice and video APIs, business messaging), contact centre as a service (TX Hub), unified communications (Microsoft Teams calling, cloud voice and SIP trunking, Kaleyra Phone), and the Commotion AI platform: Voice AI (under 250 ms latency), AI Workers (200+ templates, 500+ integrations with CRM, ERP, ITSM and HR systems) and a customer-experience platform. Scale: 60 billion+ interactions a year, 4,000+ customers, a voice network in 190+ countries. Recognition: Gartner Magic Quadrant niche player for CPaaS; Juniper Research established leader for contact centre as a service, conversational AI and mobile messaging; Omdia contact-centre leader. Customers include Flipkart, AirAsia and Yinson. Partners: Cisco, Microsoft. Sources: https://www.tatacommunications.com/kaleyra, https://www.tatacommunications.com/commotion-ai-platform Company-wide: about 5,000 enterprise customers, including 300 of the Fortune 500, in 190+ countries; part of the Tata Group.

fabrics.name: IoT
fabrics.definition: Connected devices and the intelligence on them: TCL's IoT Fabric (MOVE). Cellular IoT and eSIM / global SIM connectivity, LoRaWAN, private 4G/5G networks, embedded connectivity and MVNE services; device management, orchestration and IoT data analytics, including edge AI on devices; industry solutions for connected vehicles, logistics, aviation and manufacturing.
fabrics.tcl_today: MOVE: cellular IoT and eSIM / global SIM connectivity, embedded connectivity, MVNE services for mobile operators, LoRaWAN networks in India, private 4G/5G networks, device management and IoT data analytics; industry solutions for automotive (connected cars with JLR, and 5G in Tata Motors' Sierra.ev), logistics, aviation and manufacturing. Scale: 13 million+ SIMs managed, 160+ countries served, 600+ mobile-operator relationships. Recognition: Juniper Research leader for cellular IoT; Kaleido Intelligence champion for eSIM connectivity; 2024 AutoTech Breakthrough award. Customers include SATEL, Convergia and Fonus. Source: https://www.tatacommunications.com/move Company-wide: about 5,000 enterprise customers, including 300 of the Fortune 500, in 190+ countries; part of the Tata Group.

fabrics.name: Media
fabrics.definition: Technology for media, sport and entertainment companies: TCL's Media Fabric. Contribution and distribution of live and on-demand video over fibre, IP, satellite and cloud, including alternatives to satellite; remote and cloud production, playout and master control; media cloud, edge and storage for content workflows; low-latency video delivery networks and CDNs; live event services; fan engagement; gaming and esports infrastructure.
fabrics.tcl_today: Media Fabric, for broadcasters, sports bodies, content owners, streaming and gaming companies: media cloud and media edge, a video CDN, fibre and IP video contribution and distribution (Media Switch), remote and studio production, playout and channel origination, uplink and downlink and alternatives to satellite, live event services, fan engagement, and gaming and esports infrastructure. Scale: 70+ media cloud, edge and CDN locations; 200+ media edge compute nodes; 100,000+ events delivered, including 5,000+ remote productions; 1,000+ media hotspots in 400+ cities; 27 PB of media storage. Customers include Formula 1 (official broadcast connectivity partner), United Rugby Championship and SailGP. Recognition: Frost & Sullivan CDN radar; IDC MarketScape for commercial edge delivery and media cloud services. Source: https://www.tatacommunications.com/media-entertainment Company-wide: about 5,000 enterprise customers, including 300 of the Fortune 500, in 190+ countries; part of the Tata Group.
